subject.title: Feature: configurable mediaLocalRoots for image tool

question: Should OpenClaw solve configurable media/tool host roots through the broader tools.fs.roots policy, a narrower media-only config, or continue requiring staging into OpenClaw-managed roots?
rationale: The implementation shape changes what model-facing tools may read from the host and overlaps an open broad filesystem-root proposal, so automation should not choose the permanent trust boundary.

options.title: Adopt a central roots policy
options.body: Use a reviewed shared filesystem/media-root policy such as tools.fs.roots so image, outbound media, prompt-image loading, and filesystem tools share one operator-controlled boundary.

options.title: Add media-only roots
options.body: Create a narrower media-local-root config only if maintainers intentionally want media tools to have a separate access boundary from filesystem tools.

options.title: Keep managed staging only
options.body: Document copying, managed inbound media, and channel-scoped attachment roots as the supported path while rejecting arbitrary host-root configuration.

recommendation.title: Adopt a central roots policy
recommendation.body: Use a reviewed shared filesystem/media-root policy such as tools.fs.roots so image, outbound media, prompt-image loading, and filesystem tools share one operator-controlled boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent merged local-root policy work is the closest current-main provenance for the trust-boundary decision.
